primary_source_findings.finding: For a normal domain cgroup, cgroup.procs enumerates processes belonging to that cgroup and is not a recursive membership proof for descendant cgroups. A subtree proof therefore requires recursive descendant-cgroup enumeration or an equivalent independently complete membership source.

Threaded-domain semantics differ from ordinary domain semantics. The thread-root cgroup.procs may represent processes across the threaded subtree, while threaded children cannot be treated as ordinary domain cgroups. The witness must bind and branch on cgroup.type rather than applying one membership algorithm universally.

populated is recursively true when the cgroup or descendants contain live processes, but it is liveness evidence, not process-identity or completeness evidence. populated=1 cannot prove dedicated ownership.

The displayed cgroup path is relative to the reader's cgroup namespace root. A host-side resource witness must therefore bind the observer cgroup-namespace identity or otherwise prove it is reading from the intended host perspective before treating the path as an exact host cgroup identity.
Topology counters may be retained as sanity evidence, but descendant counts do not identify member processes and cannot replace explicit membership proof.

Podman documents hpid as the corresponding host PID of each container process and podman top displays the running processes of the named container. This provides an independent runtime-side process-set witness that can be compared with the type-correct recursive cgroup subtree membership snapshot.

refined_dedicated_subtree_gate: obtain trusted runtime-reported host main PID and bind its process incarnation
resolve exact cgroup-v2 path from that bound observer perspective
snapshot descendant cgroup topology and digest it; use type-correct recursive membership semantics
snapshot the process membership across the complete measured subtree
snapshot Podman runtime process membership using podman top <container> hpid and bind the exact container identity and observation time

compare cgroup-subtree host-PID set with the independently observed Podman host-PID set under an explicit equality/coverage rule; differences fail closed or degrade scope rather than being silently ignored
repeat or generation-fence both membership views around metric collection so process start/exit/migration races cannot silently relabel counters
only after dedicatedness and coverage are proven may readable cgroup counters be classified EXACT_CANDIDATE; otherwise preserve SUPERSET, PROCESS_SCOPED_DEGRADED, or UNKNOWN
falsifiers: any unrelated process anywhere in the measured subtree falsifies exact container attribution
omitting a descendant cgroup falsifies complete subtree membership proof
unbound observer cgroup namespace leaves /proc/<pid>/cgroup path identity ambiguous
handling a threaded cgroup as a normal domain cgroup invalidates the membership proof
using cgroup.events populated=1 as process identity or completeness evidence invalidates the proof
Podman host-PID set and cgroup-subtree host-PID set disagree outside an explicitly fenced process-lifecycle transition
a readable counter without exact scope/coverage remains non-promoting evidence

architecture_effect.trigger4_effect: Existing Trigger4 discriminator remains the sole target-runtime lane; consume this review as a contract refinement rather than creating a duplicate handoff.

resolved_previous_gap: Independent full-container host-PID enumeration is available through Podman top hpid. Exact target-runtime equivalence still requires Trigger4 to measure both sets in a bounded snapshot/fence and classify process lifecycle races rather than assume static membership.
